rationale: Mark 10:32-52 tells the same three scenes in the same order on the road to Jerusalem: the third prediction of the Passion, the request for the seats at Jesus' right and left followed by the saying on service and ransom, and a healing of blindness as they leave Jericho. Much of the wording is identical in the BSB: "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes" (Matthew 20:18; Mark 10:33); "You do not know what you are asking" (Matthew 20:22; Mark 10:38); and "did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many" (Matthew 20:28; Mark 10:45). In Greek the ransom clause is the same in every edition Bible Hub lists for both verses; only the opening differs (hosper in Matthew, kai gar in Mark). The type is parallel and the label strong, not explicit, following conn-matt16-confession-mark8: neither Gospel cites the other. The differences are checkable in the BSB. In Mark, James and John make the request themselves (10:35); in Matthew "the mother of Zebedee's sons" makes it (20:20). Mark adds "spit on Him" and "after three days" (10:34), where Matthew has "crucified" and "on the third day" (20:19). Mark has the cup and the baptism (10:38-39); Matthew has only the cup in the Greek editions the BSB follows. Mark names one blind man, "Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus" (10:46); Matthew has "two blind men" (20:30). How readers explain these differences is reported in the lesson's Positions.
